code_modification_rules.description: Rules governing code modifications by the agent
code_modification_rules.no_silent_modification: The agent MUST NOT silently modify the user's code in the background without explicit user consent. Any code change must be transparent, explicitly announced, and approved by the user before being applied. Unauthorized background modifications cause confusion and disrupt the user's workflow.
code_modification_rules.scope_of_approval: Approval is per-change. A prior approved change does not grant blanket permission for subsequent unrelated edits.
code_modification_rules.applies_to: All source files, scripts, configs, and documentation in the workspace.

command_execution_rules.description: Rules for how the agent should run commands in Trae IDE terminal

output_redirection.rule: Do NOT use bare 2>&1 redirection. Instead use 'command | tee log_<purpose>.txt' so that: (1) the AI model can read the log file afterward to analyze results, (2) the user can view real-time output in the Trae IDE terminal.
output_redirection.reason: tee gives both real-time terminal visibility for the user and a persistent log file for the AI model to read. Bare 2>&1 only goes to one place, not both.

commit_rules.description: Mandatory rules that MUST be followed before any git commit

pre_commit_testing.description: Before committing, MUST run CI batch inference test and analyze the log file to verify no regression.

ci_log_analysis.description: After running CI command, the agent MUST analyze the generated log file to verify all tests pass.
steps: 1. Extract PP and TG values from each test's common_perf_print lines
2. Verify PP and TG are valid numbers (not 'inf', 'nan', or empty)
3. Verify output text is readable (no garbled/random characters)
4. Verify output text has no repetition loops (same sentence/phrase repeated endlessly)
5. Present a summary table with pass/fail status for each test

auto_analysis_patterns.pp_tg: grep 'common_perf_print' log_ci_*.txt | grep 'prompt eval time|eval time'
auto_analysis_patterns.garbled_check: grep -c '[^[:print:]]' or manual inspection of model output lines
auto_analysis_patterns.repetition_check: visually inspect output for repeated sentence patterns (e.g. same sentence appearing 3+ times)

pp_tg_valid.description: PP and TG values must be valid numbers
pp_tg_valid.check: prompt eval time and eval time lines must contain valid numeric tokens per second values. 'inf', 'nan', or empty values indicate test failure.
pp_tg_valid.action_on_failure: Re-run the failed test. If persistent, the commit MUST NOT proceed.

no_garbled_output.description: Model output must be readable text in the expected language
no_garbled_output.check: Output should contain coherent sentences. Garbled/random characters, binary data, or unreadable symbols indicate corrupted inference.
no_garbled_output.action_on_failure: The commit MUST NOT proceed. Investigate cache coherency, tensor layout, or DSP kernel correctness.

no_repetition_loop.description: Model output must not contain endless repetition of the same sentence or phrase
no_repetition_loop.check: Scan output for the same sentence appearing 3+ times consecutively. A single repeated sentence is OK; endless looping is a bug.
no_repetition_loop.action_on_failure: The commit MUST NOT proceed. This indicates a sampling or logits corruption issue.

all_5_tests_pass.description: All 5 tests (5 models) MUST pass all 3 validation criteria above. Any single failure blocks the commit.
all_5_tests_pass.summary_table_format: | # | Model | PP (tok/s) | TG (tok/s) | Output OK | Status |

commit_message_rules.no_ai_generated: The agent MUST NOT write commit messages. The user writes the commit message.

commit_actions.reason: Commits and pushes must be explicitly performed by the user. Automated PR submissions may result in contributor ban.

ab_test.description: Performance comparison between Qualcomm's official ggml-hexagon and JZ's ggml-hexagon. For fair comparison, use the same running_params, same prompt, same LLM model file, and same phone. Reference: docs/how-to-build-ggmlhexagon.md section 'How to do performance comparison of PP and TG between Qualcomm's ggml-hexagon and JZ's ggml-hexagon'.

fair_comparison_prerequisites.same_prompt: Use the same prompt for both QCOM and JZ runs
fair_comparison_prerequisites.same_model: Use the same LLM model file for both QCOM and JZ runs
fair_comparison_prerequisites.same_phone: Use the same phone (e.g. Snapdragon 8 Elite) for both QCOM and JZ runs

automated.description: One-command automated AB test. Builds both implementations, runs both, and produces a comparison log. Best for quick regression checks.

steps.note: Already in project root directory, no need to clone. Just ensure on self-build-jz branch.
Builds with GGML_HEXAGON_JZ=OFF, using ggml-hexagon.cpp + htp/main.c
Builds with GGML_HEXAGON_JZ=ON, using ggml-hexagon-jz.cpp + htp/entry.c
Automatically runs both implementations and collects PP/TG metrics

steps.command: Analyze log_abtest_*.txt to extract PP/TG values and generate comparison table

non_automated.description: Manual step-by-step AB test. Build both implementations, then manually run llama-cli/llama-bench with each implementation by swapping libraries. Best for detailed debugging and custom prompts.

steps.note: Already in project root directory, no need to clone. Just ensure on self-build-jz branch.
Deploy QCOM libs to phone, then run llama-cli and llama-bench
Deploy JZ libs to phone, then run llama-cli and llama-bench

steps.command: Compare PP/TG values from log_llamacli_qcom.txt vs log_llamacli_jz.txt (and llama-bench logs)

key_commands_reference.update_qcom_libs: Deploy Qualcomm's .so files to phone via adb
key_commands_reference.update_jz_libs: Deploy JZ's .so files to phone via adb
key_commands_reference.run_abtest: Run automated AB test (builds + runs both, outputs comparison)
key_commands_reference.run_llamacli: Run llama-cli with currently deployed libs
key_commands_reference.run_llamabench: Run llama-bench with currently deployed libs

build_forbidden.reason: Follow ONLY docs/how-to-build-ggmlhexagon.md. Ignore all toplevel build files.

script_rules.reason: All functions are allowed for local execution.

dsp_kernel_fast_build.description: If only DSP-side source files (under ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/, e.g. entry.c, matmul-ops.c, HVX/HMX kernels) were modified, use the fast kernel-only build to skip the full AP rebuild.
dsp_kernel_fast_build.when_to_use: Only DSP-side files in ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/ were modified; no changes to ARM-AP source (ggml-hexagon.cpp, ggml-hexagon-jz.cpp) or top-level build files.
dsp_kernel_fast_build.fallback: If any AP-side file (ggml-hexagon.cpp, ggml-hexagon-jz.cpp) or non-DSP file was also modified, fall back to the full build command above.

build_rules.cifs_check: Check whether the project is located on a CIFS file system and modify ./scripts/build-run-ggmlhexagon-android.sh accordingly
build_rules.if_unsure: STOP. Do NOT use make/cmake. ONLY follow: docs/how-to-build-ggmlhexagon.md

do_not_modify.reason: These files are maintained as part of the project infrastructure. Modify with caution and follow project conventions.

notes.execution_mode: local (no ssh needed - project is on local filesystem)
notes.phone_connected_locally: adb connects to the Android phone locally
notes.compare_with_qcom: To compare against Qualcomm's official ggml-hexagon backend, run: ./scripts/build-run-ggmlhexagon-android.sh build_qcom

hexagon_implementations.description: Two ggml-hexagon implementations share the same DSP kernel directory (htp/) but use different ARM-AP source files AND different DSP entry-point source files. The bulk of htp/ (ops kernels, HVX/HMX headers, common headers) is shared, but the DSP-side entry-point main function lives in different files.

qualcomm_official.description: Qualcomm's official ggml-hexagon implementation. AP side: ggml-hexagon.cpp. DSP entry point: htp/main.c. DSP ops/HVX/HMX: shared htp/ directory.

jz_implementation.description: JZ's custom ggml-hexagon implementation (primary development target). AP side: ggml-hexagon-jz.cpp. DSP entry point: htp/entry.c. DSP ops/HVX/HMX: shared htp/ directory.

hexagon_implementations.shared_dsp_directory_note: Both implementations compile DSP ops kernels, HVX/HMX headers, and common helpers from the shared htp/ directory. They differ in: (1) ARM-AP source file - ggml-hexagon.cpp vs ggml-hexagon-jz.cpp, selected by CMake option GGML_HEXAGON_JZ (default OFF); (2) DSP entry-point source file - htp/main.c (QCOM) vs htp/entry.c (JZ).

jz_implementation.description: JZ's custom ggml-hexagon implementation (primary development target). AP side: ggml-hexagon-jz.cpp. DSP entry point: htp/entry.c. DSP ops/HVX/HMX: shared htp/ directory.

qualcomm_official_debug.description: Qualcomm's official backend. AP side: ggml-hexagon.cpp. DSP entry point: htp/main.c. DSP ops/HVX/HMX: shared htp/ directory. Use this when debugging or benchmarking against the official reference.

ccache_usage.description: ccache is enabled for faster builds. For jz build: CCACHE_DIR=${PROJECT_ROOT_PATH}/.ccache. For qcom build: CCACHE_DIR=${PROJECT_ROOT_PATH}/.ccache_qcom. Do NOT disable ccache.

testing_rules.description: Test commands for different test types. All tests should be run locally.
testing_rules.note: All tests must be executed locally

log_viewing_rules.description: How to view logs (execute locally on this machine)

ut_program_log.note: Use this to debug UT program issues, test failures, and ARM-AP side errors

dsp_log.note: Use this to debug DSP-side issues, including DSP crashes, memory issues, and HMX/HVX instruction errors

log_viewing_rules.workflow: After running a test, always check the relevant log to understand what happened. If UT fails, check ut_program_log first. If DSP crashes or produces incorrect results, check dsp_log.
